records.name: Women in Healthcare, Greater Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: A networking and learning group for women who work in healthcare administration, operations and facilities in the Philadelphia area. The group offers networking, learning and mentoring for its members.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member to take part in chapter networking, education and mentoring, or sign up for the email list to hear what is coming up.

cost.text: Dues are not published on the page

first_step.how: Use the Join Now button on the chapter site to start a membership, or sign up for the email list
first_step.basis: Joining takes a membership sign-up and dues are not published, so the first step is not clear without applying

records.notes: IRS legal name Women in Healthcare Inc. The batch website had a www prefix that does not resolve, so the bare subdomain was read. No dated events or news on the home page. The newest item found is a 2026 sponsorship page with no month, so status is probably_active. The calendar link carries an August 2021 start date. Email was read from the protected contact link. Phone is a 302 (Delaware area code) number as published; confirm.

records.name: Woodcrest Housing Inc
records.notes: Website is Mission First Housing Group, a housing developer and property manager. Its office address (2042-48 Arch Street, 2nd floor) matches the IRS filing, but the page never names Woodcrest Housing. Public ways in are a newsletter, donations, job listings and a yearly fundraiser (Welcome Home 2026, Wednesday October 14, at the Free Library of Philadelphia, per the site). A veterans gift drive and resident services are listed with no details. Verdict is a judgment call: it is a housing business rather than a membership or volunteer group. Owner may flip it to publish if housing developers belong in the directory.

records.name: The Youth Sexpert Program
records.summary: A nonprofit that trains young people to be sexual health peer educators, so they can share accurate information with friends and classmates. Training covers consent, body knowledge and reducing stigma around STIs.
records.what_you_do: Young people take part in a training cohort and become peer educators. The program also offers intensives and takes donations.

cost.text: No cost or fee listed on the homepage; the cohort application gives no details

first_step.how: Fill in the Fall 2026 youth cohort application linked from theyouthsexpertprogram.org
first_step.basis: Young people join through an application for a cohort, and the page gives no deadline or cohort details

records.notes: The only dated item is the Fall 2026 cohort application, with no month, so status is probably_active. Email and phone are on the Contact page, which was not read. Instagram, LinkedIn and Facebook links exist, but their addresses were not captured. Ages served are not published. The partner organizations named on the site are national groups, so they are not added as leads.

records.name: Zia: Food You Can Count On
records.summary: A charity that brings healthy food to Philadelphia schoolchildren and their families. It runs a pantry for about forty families at one city school, and volunteers pack and deliver meals each week.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers pack and deliver meals weekly. Families can ask about joining the pantry, and anyone can give through the donate page.

schedule.text: Volunteers pack and deliver meals each week. The page gives no days or times.

cost.text: Not stated for volunteers or families; online donations are accepted

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer With Us page on ziafood.org, or send a message through Contact Us
first_step.basis: The site has a clear volunteer page and invites new volunteers, but it does not describe what a first shift is like

records.notes: The IRS filing address is a private apartment, so no location is recorded and the school is not named on the page. The Press Releases page is linked but shows no entries; the only date is a 2026 copyright, which does not count. Email and phone are on the Contact Us page, which was not read. Social handles as shown on the site: Facebook Ziafoodphilly and Instagram ziafoodyoucancounty. The page publishes no eligibility rules for member families.

cost.text: Membership fees are not published on the pages read

first_step.how: Check the events page at caccc.us for the next workshop or networking event, or fill in the membership application
first_step.basis: Membership pages exist, but the site does not say whether workshops and networking events are open to people who are not members

records.name: IBOA International Basketball Officials Academy
records.summary: A Philadelphia program that teaches FIBA 3x3 basketball to young people through clinics, camps and tournaments, including sessions at city recreation centers. It also trains and mentors basketball referees.
records.what_you_do: Kids and teens can take part in 3x3 clinics, camps and tournaments when they run. Adults can volunteer through the volunteer form on the site.

schedule.text: Clinics, camps and tournaments are announced through the newsletter. The page gives no days, times or dates.

cost.text: Prices are not published on the page

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on iboa3x3.com to hear when the next youth clinic or camp opens, or send the volunteer form from the Become a Volunteer page
first_step.basis: Youth programs are for young people and there is a clear sign-up for the newsletter and for volunteering, but registration steps for clinics are not published

records.notes: The batch website was typed as httpa://www.iboa3x3.com and was read at https://www.iboa3x3.com. The only 2026 evidence is a cut-off photo caption about a 2026 NACLA Cup, with no month, so status is probably_active. The Cup has no date on the page. Referee education runs from iboaofficials.org, a sister site of the same academy, which was not read and is not recorded separately. The IRS filing shows an apartment address (2650 Welsh Rd Apt 21); the public office address is used.

records.name: Delaware Valley Fly Fishers
records.summary: A club for fly anglers and fly tiers from around the Delaware Valley. Members learn casting, fly tying and fishing, go on day and multi-day fishing trips, and take part in conservation and education work.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly meeting as a guest, take a beginner fly fishing or fly tying class, or join to get the newsletter, member classes and trips.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting at 7 pm on the second Thursday, with no December meeting. Beginner classes run over several weeks.

cost.text: Dues and class fees are not listed on the page; check the membership application

first_step.how: Come to the second Thursday meeting at 7 pm at Churchville Nature Center as a guest, or sign up for the Beginner Fly Fishing or Beginner Fly Tying class
first_step.basis: The club runs beginner fly fishing and fly tying classes, and guests are welcome at the monthly meeting

records.notes: IRS legal name is International Federation of Fly Fishers Inc, also listed as Delaware Valley Fly Fishers 1. The website is the club's own; the club is a charter club of Fly Fishers International. It meets in Churchville, Bucks County, not in Philadelphia, but serves anglers from the wider Delaware Valley, so in_city is false. Owner may decide whether regional clubs belong. No exact fishing tag exists; river_stewardship is the closest fit and fly tying is filed under craft_circle. Two email addresses appear on the site and the page text did not make clear which is current, so none is recorded. Dated items: a September 2026 past event, an October 2026 newsletter, and a November 2026 upcoming event.

records.name: AfterShock Fam
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs music and arts workshops for kids, including DJ, beatmaking and music production camps, and pairs young people with one-on-one mentors. It also connects artists who want to mentor.
records.what_you_do: Kids and families can join workshops. Kids who have attended one can be matched with online one-on-one mentoring. Artists can join the Creative Network after mentor training.

schedule.text: Camps and workshops are listed by date. The newest listed DJ Cafe sessions were in late 2024, and no current dates appear on the pages read. Music camps for ages 8 to 16 are listed for July, with no year on the page.

locations.label: DJ Cafe site (as listed for 2024 sessions)

cost.text: No prices are listed on the pages read

first_step.how: Ask about the next DJ Cafe, BeatCamp or mentoring spot through the contact page at aftershockfam.org/contact-us/
first_step.basis: Kids can join workshops, but the listed dates are from 2024 and the page does not say how to sign up

records.notes: The newest dated listing is a DJ Cafe session on December 4, 2024, so status is probably_active at best. BeatCamp and Music Maker's Discovery Camp have no year on the page, and a 2022 tour is old. Social links on the site are placeholders with no addresses. The owner or a later check should confirm which programs run now.
